name: Espresso Macchiato
intro: An espresso macchiato is a shot of espresso 'marked' with just a spoonful of foamed milk. It stays bold and intense, with the foam softening the edge slightly and adding a touch of sweetness. It's perfect when you want milk's mellowness without losing the espresso.
heroAlt: Engraved line illustration of an espresso macchiato with a dollop of foam

vessel.name: Espresso cup (demitasse), pre-warmed
vessel.note: A small cup keeps the proportions right.

ingredients.note: From roughly 18 g of finely ground coffee.
Thick, spoonable foam from a small amount of milk.

equipment.alternative: Moka pot or AeroPress plus a handheld frother (see home methods)

steps.title: Warm the cup
steps.body: Preheat a small cup with hot water. An espresso macchiato is a small drink, and a warm cup keeps it from cooling too quickly.

steps.title: Pull the shot
steps.body: Pull a double shot straight into the cup. The crema should look rich and golden, since it's the base for the foam.
steps.tip: Pull the shot right before you make the foam so it's fresh.

steps.title: Froth a little milk
steps.body: Pour a small amount of cold milk, about 2 to 3 oz, into a small pitcher so you can froth properly. The extra milk is easier to steam well, and you'll only use a spoonful of the foam.
steps.tip: If you have no steam wand, use a handheld frother in a mug.

steps.title: Build thick foam
steps.body: Add plenty of air at the start to make stiff, creamy foam, then heat to around 140°F. Thick foam sits on top of the espresso instead of sinking, which gives the drink its 'mark'.
steps.tip: Tap and swirl until it looks glossy but holds its shape.

steps.title: Spoon on the foam
steps.body: Use a teaspoon to scoop about 1 tbsp of foam and dollop it in the center of the espresso. Don't stir, as the contrast between the foam and the shot is part of the experience.

steps.title: Sip right away
steps.body: Drink it while the foam is warm and the espresso is still hot. A few sips is all it takes.

homeMethods.note: Pour a small moka pot brew into a cup and top with foam from a handheld frother. It's bold and a good home version, but the coffee is less concentrated and has no crema.
A strong, fine-grind AeroPress shot works well. Add a dollop of foamed milk. The foam holds, but the shot is cleaner and lighter than real espresso.
A small cup of very strong coffee with a spoon of frothed milk captures the spirit but not the intensity. Expect a milder result.

tips: Use fresh whole milk for the best, thickest foam.
Don't stir it, so you can enjoy the layers.
In some countries, 'macchiato' can mean a larger milk-based drink, so definitions vary by café and region.
commonMistakes: Adding too much milk and turning it into a cortado or small latte.
Making foam that's too thin to sit on top.

variations.name: Latte macchiato
variations.description: The reverse: espresso poured into a tall glass of steamed milk.

variations.name: Single-shot macchiato
variations.description: Uses one shot of espresso instead of a double.

variations.name: Cortado
variations.description: Espresso with a roughly equal amount of warm milk. It's milder than a macchiato.

history: 'Macchiato' means 'marked' or 'stained' in Italian, referring to the espresso being marked with milk. The exact origin of the drink is unclear.

seo.title: How to Make an Espresso Macchiato: Espresso Marked with Foam
seo.description: Make a classic espresso macchiato with a double shot and 1 tbsp of foamed milk. Includes easy home methods without an espresso machine.
